task.prompt:
ROLE: independent binding DESIGN reviewer for Foundation C slice C3b, stage R3 (default-OFF
execution cell runner + bwrap). Read-only — no edits/commits. DESIGN review (no code). This is the
first ENFORCEMENT-TIER C3b stage — hold it to the highest bar; R3 build additionally requires
single-use owner activation. You substitute for codex (usage-limited to Aug 4; codex confirmatory
on return). VERIFY claims against real code/system — do not approve prose; do not fabricate.

READ:
- .agents/plans/aqos-foundation-c/C3B-R3-DESIGN-AND-AUTHORIZATION.md (under review)
- R0/R1/R2 (C3B-DESIGN, C3B-R1-DESIGN, C3B-R2-DESIGN) — R3 composes R1 verify + R2 clone
- Ground against real code/system: nix/modules/services/switchboard.nix (RestrictNamespaces=true:534,
  NoNewPrivileges:526-ish, User:519 — must stay byte-for-byte), nix/modules/services/default.nix
  (import point), ai-stack/switchboard/capability_lease_gate.py (resolve_current_epoch),
  scripts/ai/lib/execution_grant.py (R1 verify_grant — public-key-only), scripts/ai/lib/execution_cell_clone.py
  (R2 create_cell, IF present). Host userns: `unshare --user` works and /proc/sys/user/
  max_user_namespaces is non-zero (the design claims no global userns change is needed — verify this reasoning).

TEST THESE OBLIGATIONS (§10) — CLOSED or concrete gap w/ §ref + fix:
1. Runner is the ONLY userns holder; switchboard.nix hardening byte-for-byte unchanged; NO global
   security.unprivilegedUsernsClone change (is the §2 claim that the host already permits unprivileged
   userns correct, and is scoping RestrictNamespaces to CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNS on the runner unit
   sufficient for bwrap while keeping the switchboard untouched)?
2. UDS transport-only; SO_PEERCRED enforced; no error oracle; conveys no authority.
3. Grant verified by R1 with PUBLIC key only (compromised runner cannot forge); deny-closed;
   authority-degrade → safe-read only.
4. bwrap argv derived ONLY from the verified grant; --unshare-all + --unshare-net deny-all egress;
   single writable = cell root; no live .git/home/secret/device; --clearenv+allowlist; NO unsandboxed
   fallback (aider AI_AIDER_SANDBOX_FALLBACK_UNSAFE explicitly forbidden). Any bwrap arg that leaks host?
5. Supervision (§6): 250ms epoch/liveness poll, runner-generated heartbeat (caller heartbeats never
   trusted), cgroup whole-tree SIGTERM→cgroup.kill→prove-absence-or-QUARANTINE, FINAL epoch fence
   before GREEN. Any race where a revoked/epoch-bumped cell publishes GREEN, or a subprocess escapes the cgroup?
6. Out-of-cell validator (§7): ignores ALL cell-controlled git config/hooks/attributes/textconv;
   compares bytes/modes/symlinks against trusted base; declared-signed-paths-only; any deviation → RED.
7. No auto-merge; GREEN only retains a diff for separate review.
8. Nix (§8): runner-only scoped RestrictNamespaces + NoNewPrivileges + empty caps + ProtectSystem=strict
   + StateDirectory; flag default OFF + env-contract; switchboard byte-parity asserted.
9. Scope: no switchboard adoption (R5), no network (C4), no live traffic, no perf-gate numeric claim (R4).

ALSO: any NEW fail-open or confinement-escape? Is the R2→R3 handoff clean? Weigh Q-R3-1 (persistent
runner vs systemd-run transient), Q-R3-2 (validator confinement), Q-R3-3 (cgroup v2 delegation for an
unprivileged runner — is Delegate= enough for cgroup.kill without extra privilege?), Q-R3-4 (bounded
command-descriptor vocabulary = noop/read-validate/single-file-write only for R3?).

OUTPUT: `VERDICT: PASS` / `VERDICT: FAIL` / `VERDICT: REQUEST_REVISION` on the FIRST line, then
findings by severity (BLOCKING/SHOULD-FIX/NICE-TO-HAVE) with exact §ref + concrete fix, and verdicts
on Q-R3-1..4. No review outcome authorizes build or activation.
